course_outcomes: Explain core machine‑learning concepts and terminology
Prepare and explore data using Python and SQL
Build, train, and evaluate simple supervised models with Scikit‑Learn
Apply model validation techniques and basic hyperparameter tuning
Demonstrate foundational MLOps practices by packaging and deploying a model

modules.module_title: Foundations of Machine Learning & Python Refresher
topics: What is Machine Learning? Scope and applications
Types of learning: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement
Python environment setup (conda, virtualenv)
Core Python libraries: NumPy, pandas overview
Basic data structures for ML
learning_outcomes: Define machine learning and differentiate its main categories
Set up a reproducible Python environment for ML projects
Import and use NumPy and pandas for numerical and tabular data
suggested_resources: Chapter 1 of "Hands‑On Machine Learning with Scikit‑Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow"

modules.module_title: Data Exploration & SQL for Machine Learning
topics: Loading data from CSV, Excel, and databases
Data cleaning: handling missing values, outliers, and type conversion
Introduction to relational databases and basic SQL syntax
Connecting Python to SQL with SQLAlchemy and pandas.read_sql
Exploratory data analysis (EDA) visualizations
learning_outcomes: Import datasets into pandas DataFrames from files and SQL tables
Perform common cleaning operations and summarize data
Write basic SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY queries to retrieve training data
suggested_resources: Kaggle “Intro to SQL for Data Science” course

topics: Regression fundamentals and assumptions
Cost function and gradient descent intuition
Scikit‑Learn LinearRegression API
Training, prediction, and coefficient interpretation
Evaluation metrics: MSE, RMSE, MAE
learning_outcomes: Build a linear regression model with scikit‑learn
Calculate and report regression error metrics
suggested_resources: Chapter 3 of "Hands‑On Machine Learning with Scikit‑Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow"

topics: Binary classification concepts
Logistic regression theory and scikit‑learn implementation
k‑Nearest Neighbors algorithm and distance metrics
Train‑test split, stratification
Confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, F1‑score
learning_outcomes: Implement logistic regression and k‑NN classifiers
Evaluate classification performance using confusion matrix and derived metrics
Choose appropriate classifier for a given binary problem
suggested_resources: Kaggle “Intro to Machine Learning” notebook on classification
Towards Data Science article on evaluation metrics

topics: Overfitting vs. underfitting
k‑fold cross‑validation and stratified folds
GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV
Feature scaling with StandardScaler
Building pipelines to streamline preprocessing and modeling
learning_outcomes: Apply k‑fold cross‑validation to estimate model generalization
Create a scikit‑learn pipeline that includes scaling and model steps
suggested_resources: Machine Learning Mastery article on Grid Search

topics: Model serialization with joblib and pickle
Building a simple REST API using Flask
Version control basics for ML assets (Git)
Monitoring basics and ethical considerations
Overview of CI/CD concepts for ML (MLflow, DVC)
learning_outcomes: Save a trained model to disk and reload it for inference
Create a minimal Flask API that serves predictions
Explain the key steps of an MLOps workflow and why they matter
suggested_resources: Google Cloud “MLOps: Continuous Delivery and Automation” video

project_ideas: Predict house prices using a public real‑estate dataset (linear regression, feature engineering, and model evaluation)
Build a churn‑prediction classifier for a telecom dataset, including data cleaning, hyperparameter tuning, and a Flask prediction endpoint
Create a simple recommendation system that suggests movies based on user ratings, using k‑NN and deploying the model as an API

industry_skill_alignment.alignment_summary: The curriculum weaves core industry‑demanded skills into every week: Python and SQL are used for data acquisition and preparation; Scikit‑Learn provides hands‑on experience building and tuning models; rigorous evaluation methods mirror real‑world performance monitoring; and the final week introduces MLOps concepts such as model serialization, API deployment, and version control, ensuring graduates are ready to contribute to data‑driven teams from day one.
